# California Café Lease Risk Snapshot

This fact pattern has several **common lease risk points** for a small café tenant in California, especially around **personal liability, repair obligations, and the tenant improvement allowance**. The main practical goal is to identify what to clarify before signing and what a lawyer should review in the final draft.

# Key Lease Issues to Review Before Signing

| Issue | Why it matters | What to ask a lawyer |
|---|---|---|
| Personal guarantee | Can expose the owner’s personal assets if the business defaults | Can the guarantee be limited in time, amount, or tied to a “good guy” exit? |
| HVAC repair clause | HVAC can be expensive and may include major system failures, not just routine service | Does “repairs” include replacement, compressor failure, or only maintenance? |
| Security deposit of USD 9,600 | Equal to 2 months’ rent, so refund rules and use of funds matter | When can the landlord apply it, and is it refundable within a set time? |
| Tenant improvement allowance of USD 12,000 | May come with reimbursement deadlines, lien waivers, or approval conditions | What proof is needed, who approves work, and when is the allowance paid? |
| 3-year term | Mid-term flexibility matters if the café underperforms | Is there an early termination right, assignment right, or sublease option? |
| Use as a café | Food-service use can trigger permitting, grease, venting, ADA, and health-code issues | Is the space legally permitted for café use and required exhaust/plumbing? |

# Practical Checklist for Your Pre-Sign Review

- **Lease term and exit rights**
  - Confirm the exact start date, expiration date, and any renewal options.
  - Ask whether there is any right to terminate early, assign, or sublease.
  - Check for automatic rent increases during the 3-year term.

- **Personal guarantee**
  - Review whether the guarantee is full, limited, or continuing after lease expiration.
  - Ask if it can be capped at a dollar amount or limited to a shorter period.
  - Confirm whether it covers rent only or also damages, attorney fees, and repair costs.

- **Rent and deposit economics**
  - Verify base rent, due dates, late fees, grace period, and any percentage rent.
  - Check how the **USD 9,600** deposit can be used and when it must be returned.
  - Ask whether the deposit can be reduced after on-time payment history.

- **HVAC responsibility**
  - Separate **routine maintenance** from **major repair** and **replacement**.
  - Ask who pays for pre-existing HVAC defects or end-of-life equipment.
  - Confirm whether service contracts, filters, and annual inspections are required.

- **Tenant improvement allowance**
  - Confirm whether the **USD 12,000** is paid upfront or reimbursed after completion.
  - Check deadlines for completion, invoice submission, and landlord approval.
  - Ask whether lien releases are required from contractors before payment.

- **Permits and café buildout**
  - Confirm the space is approved for restaurant/café use under zoning and the lease.
  - Review who is responsible for health permits, fire compliance, ADA items, grease trap, and ventilation.
  - Check whether any buildout work needs landlord consent before starting.

- **Operating costs and pass-throughs**
  - Look for CAM charges, property tax pass-throughs, insurance reimbursements, and utility obligations.
  - Ask for the prior year’s operating expense history if available.
  - Confirm whether trash, water, pest control, and grease disposal are tenant costs.

- **Insurance requirements**
  - Review required policy types, limits, and whether the landlord must be an additional insured.
  - Check if liquor, food contamination, or business interruption coverage is required.
  - Confirm whether the lease requires waiver of subrogation.

- **Default and remedies**
  - Read the default notice period and cure rights carefully.
  - Ask what remedies the landlord has after default, including lockout, acceleration, or attorney fees.
  - Check whether personal guarantee liability starts immediately upon default.

- **Condition of the premises**
  - Document the current condition with photos and a move-in inspection.
  - Ask for representations about code compliance, roof, plumbing, electrical, and HVAC condition.
  - Confirm whether there is any prior water damage, mold, or unpermitted work.

# Questions to Ask Your Lawyer

- Is the **personal guarantee** negotiable, and can it be limited or released after a period of good performance?
- Does the HVAC clause make the tenant responsible for **major replacement** or only routine service and minor repairs?
- Is the **tenant improvement allowance** protected if the landlord delays approval or reimbursement?
- Are there any California-specific issues with this lease structure, including enforceability of default remedies and deposit handling?
- Does the lease clearly state the space is suitable and permitted for **café operations**?
- Are there hidden costs in CAM, insurance, utilities, or repair obligations that materially change the economics?
- Should we require a **move-in condition report** and a landlord repair schedule before signing?
